back: Verify explicitly, use least-privilege access, assume breach — trust is never granted by network location.
Layered protections — physical, identity, perimeter, network, compute, app, data — so one breached layer meets the next.
Encryption is reversible with a key (data at rest/in transit). Hashing is an irreversible fingerprint — how passwords are stored.
Governance sets the rules, risk management handles what could go wrong, compliance proves external obligations are met.
AuthN proves who you are; AuthZ decides what you may do once proven.
Creates, maintains, and verifies identities and issues tokens applications trust — Entra ID is Microsoft's.
Trust between identity providers so one organisation's users access another's resources with their home accounts.
Microsoft's cloud identity and access management service — the IdP behind Azure, Microsoft 365, and integrated apps.
Users (humans), workload identities (apps/services — service principals, managed identities), devices, and agent ID for AI agents.
On-premises AD accounts synchronised with Entra ID — one identity on-premises and in the cloud.
Something you know (password/PIN) + have (phone, key) + are (biometric) — two or more different categories.
Windows Hello for Business, FIDO2 security keys, passkeys — no password exists to phish or leak.
Banned-password lists (global + custom), smart lockout, and self-service password reset.
Sign-in policy engine: signals (user, location, device, app, risk) → decision (allow, require MFA, block).
Built-in directory roles assigned at least privilege. Entra roles govern the identity platform; Azure RBAC governs Azure resources.
Just-in-time role activation: eligible instead of permanent, time-bound, optionally approval-gated.
Detects identity risks (leaked credentials, impossible travel), scores user and sign-in risk, and can drive automated Conditional Access responses.
Recurring human recertification of group memberships, app access, and roles — access expires with its purpose.
Bundles resources — groups, apps, sites — into access packages that users can request, with approval and expiry built in, so access is granted as a package rather than item by item.

front: Azure Firewall vs WAF vs NSG
back: Firewall: managed stateful network filtering across VNets. WAF: blocks HTTP-level exploits (SQLi, XSS). NSG: subnet/NIC-level allow-deny rules.
RDP/SSH to VMs through the portal over TLS — no public IPs or exposed management ports.
Safeguarded store for secrets, keys, and certificates — retrieved at runtime under access policy and audit.
Absorbs volumetric denial-of-service floods before they reach applications.
Continuous configuration assessment against standards, recommendations, and Secure Score to measure posture.
Defender for Cloud's active half: threat detection and hardening for servers, storage, databases, containers.
SIEM collects, correlates, detects across the estate. SOAR automates the response with playbooks. Sentinel is both, cloud-native.
Protects email and collaboration: phishing, malicious links and attachments in Exchange, Teams, SharePoint.
Device protection: EDR, attack surface reduction, automated investigation on laptops, servers, mobile.
Cloud access security broker: discovers shadow IT, governs SaaS usage, protects data across cloud apps.
Watches on-premises Active Directory for identity attacks — reconnaissance, credential theft, lateral movement.
The unified home where incidents from the Defender family correlate into single coordinated investigations.
Keeps management ports closed and opens them only for an approved user, for a limited window, from a limited source — shrinking the window an exposed port is attackable.
The integrations that pull logs into Microsoft Sentinel from Microsoft services, other clouds, and on-premises sources. Without connectors a SIEM has nothing to correlate.
A measure of an organisation's security posture against recommended configuration, with prioritised improvement actions and progress over time.
Microsoft's public evidence locker: audit reports, certifications, and documentation of its own compliance.
Control, transparency, security, strong legal protections, no content-based targeting, benefits to you.
Assessments map configuration to regulations with improvement actions; compliance score measures progress.
Classify content and enforce travelling protection — encryption, watermarks, access restrictions.
Policies that detect sensitive content in motion and warn, block, or audit the risky action.
Retention policies/labels keep-then-delete on schedule; records management makes declared records immutable with reviewed disposition.
Correlates internal signals (mass downloads, pre-departure activity) into pseudonymised, investigable cases.
eDiscovery searches and legal-holds content for cases; audit records who did what, where, when across Microsoft 365.
Purview's view of what sensitive content exists and where, built from sensitive information types and trainable classifiers — the input every protection policy depends on.
Detects policy violations in internal messaging — harassment, regulatory breaches, sensitive data sharing — and routes them for review.
The Purview data governance experience for cataloguing data assets across sources, so owners, quality, and lineage are recorded in one place.
Microsoft's privacy risk management and subject rights request tooling — finding personal data, spotting privacy risk, and handling requests from data subjects.
